content:
maria: Heads-up — saw a reproducible OOM pattern on paged-attn when we hit a mixed-batch workload (long + short sequences). Dumping notes here so we can iterate on allocator/eviction heuristics.

alex: can you paste the perf output? is this during canary or prod? :thinking:

maria: canary. workload: 60% seq512, 40% seq64, models: mix of 7B/13B variants. Repro steps: 1) warm-up with seq64 steady, 2) flood with concurrent seq512 streams, 3) occasional route to 13B fallback. Failure window ~30s after flood.

ryan: two likely suspects: workspace oversubscription (kernel temp buffers) or KV block compaction thrash. Which one dominates?

maria: nvprof-ish sampling attached below (snip). Key lines:
```
nsys: gpu_mem_peak: 21.1GB (device total 24GB)
block_mgr.allocate: 9.2GB
kv_cache.resident: 6.4GB
workspace.temp_peak: 7.5GB
compaction.pass_time: 120ms avg spikes to 850ms during OOM
```
I think compaction latency spikes coincide with kernel scheduling backlog which pushes temporary workspace above soft cap.

lee: interesting — compaction spike -> longer longest-running kernel -> other streams' `workspace` can't free in time -> we queue more temp buffers -> OOM. Have we tried pre-emptive compaction (background thread) vs synchronous compaction?

maria: yes. Background compaction reduced wall-time for some runs but shifted the window (still saw OOMs) because background compaction competes for workspace with active kernels. We don't currently account for background compaction in kernel selection / workspace reservation.

sophia: is kernel selection making choices that assume available workspace = free_mem - kv_resident? maybe selecting larger-favored kernels (fast but high-temp) for seq512 which amplifies frag.

alex: exactly. Example: for attention we pick the kernel variant with lower per-token compute (better latency) but uses bigger temporary GEMM buffers for fused matmuls. On mixed loads that increases `workspace.temp_peak` variance.

ryan: proposal: two-pronged experiment set — allocator tuning + eviction heuristic change. Summary:
1) fix a "workspace headroom" fraction for each stream (e.g., reserve 12% of device mem for emergency workspace)
2) change block manager to prefer smaller block_size (256->128) to reduce compaction cost latency at the expense of more metadata
3) add an eviction policy that considers "compaction cost" score not just LRU time (score = stale_bytes * estimated_compaction_ms)
4) make kernel selector aware of current temporary workspace pressure and reject high-temp variants above threshold (fallback to slower, low-temp variant)

lee: I like 4 — kernel selector as adaptive fallbacks. We already have a multi-variant table, just need runtime signals. What's the metric cadence? per-batch? per-ms?

maria: per-dispatch check (cheap): read atomic workspace_footprint counter and compare to high-water threshold. If > threshold, set `prefer_low_temp=true` for this dispatch.

sophia: for 2 (smaller block size) we should simulate metadata blowup: estimate extra bucket count and added pointer overhead. If overhead > 1% of device mem then reject. We need numbers.

alex: did a quick calc: current block_size=256 -> avg resident_blocks 25k -> metadata ~ 25k * 16B = 400KB. If we move to 128, resident_blocks ~ 45k -> metadata ~ 720KB. negligible. The real cost is fragmentation: smaller block granularity reduces compaction passes but increases total tracked entries and per-alloc overhead.

maria: ran a short AB test (canary branch) with these knobs: `workspace_headroom=10%`, `block_size=128`, `evict_score_threshold=0.25`, `kernel_temp_limit=0.65*device_free_workspace`. Results (summary):
```
baseline: 3 OOMs / 1000 requests
experiment A: 0 OOMs / 1000 requests
p99 latency: +7ms for seq512 (kernel fallback)
avg compaction latency: from 120ms -> 32ms
throughput delta: -3% overall
```
So fewer OOMs and compaction latency down but small perf hit.

ryan: nice! Do you have flamegraph/profile showing where compaction time went?

maria: yes — compaction syscall/memcpy was dominating in baseline. In experiment we still had compaction but evenly spaced. I can paste the short perf dump:
```
baseline compaction timeline: [0–5s] 3 spikes: 450ms, 780ms, 610ms -> kernels queuing
expA compaction timeline: [0–5s] 12 small passes: 30–40ms each -> no queue
```

lee: that's exactly the kind of behavior we want to avoid. So shorter, more frequent compactions wins. But what about worst-case memory blowups with a large long sequence burst? The headroom might be consumed quickly.

sophia: consider a proactive admission control: if headroom < safety_margin (e.g., < 6%) we throttle new long-seq dispatches and bump routing to smaller model variant or queued rate-limit token-gen. Could be enabled only for dedicated nodes.

alex: one more angle — KV cache sticky allocation. We currently allocate blocks on-demand and mark them resident; hot keys cause contiguous resident runs which are heavy to compact. If we bias block allocation to scatter hot keys across buckets (hash-with-stride) compaction becomes cheaper because freed blocks are more uniformly distributed. Might cost a bit more on hit semantics (more misses) but reduces compaction passes.

maria: implemented a prototype `scatter_alloc` in blockmgr and ran with same AB test. Results: compaction passes reduced 18%, metadata churn up slightly, and p99 latency stable. Good candidate for next iteration.

ryan: next steps (action items):
- maria: push canary branch with workspace_headroom and kernel-selector hook behind feature flag (ETA EOD)
- alex: add small simulator to estimate blockmgr metadata growth for block_size choices (help sophia)
- sophia: define eviction scoring function and simulate traces to pick good threshold
- lee: sketch admission-control webhook that lives in router for dedicated nodes (we can use existing token-bucket infra)

maria: I'll also capture a short reproducer script (docker-compose canary image) and include `nsys` capture link. Will tag infra-bot to deploy experiment flag for the canary pool.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: canary-pool flag=workspace_headroom_experiment by maria. CI pipeline link: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234

alex: great. one last thought — let's add a short-run test in our nightly perf suite that mixes seq64/512/1024 at 60/30/10 to catch regressions early. Otherwise we keep discovering this in prod.

maria: agreed. I'll add the test and update the perf-alerting rule for compaction_spike > 300ms.

ryan: cool. thanks all, this felt productive. We'll iterate on thresholds after more canary data. :thumbsup:
